title: Policy Scripting Sandbox - UX notes & wireframe writeup
body:
Context:
Quick notes for the interactive Policy Scripting Sandbox (PSS) — goal: let operators author, preview, and test rollout/fallback policies without shipping to prod. Target personas: platform engineers who operate Dedicated/Private tenants and product PMs who define canary/A-B campaigns.

Problem statement:
- Existing rollout editor is form-heavy and brittle for complex fallback chains (region + model variant + cost-tier).
- Hard to preview traffic behavior for nested match conditions and time-based ramps.
- Engineers want an immediate test harness to run synthetic traffic and validate metrics/guardrails before saving.

Design goals (high level):
- Dual-mode editor: visual flow builder + code DSL (sync both ways).
- Fast preview: run N synthetic requests, show distribution, latency/cost model, and QA flags.
- Safety: linting + simulated canary impact estimate + one-click generate rollback policy.
- Reusability: policies can be saved as templates, parameterized for team-level defaults.

Wireframe notes (screen-by-screen):
1) Landing: Policy library (left pane) / Selected policy summary (center) / Quick actions (right): run preview, clone, publish, history. Secondary: filter by tag (canary, a/b, fallback), by team, by model family.

2) Editor: Top bar: name + environment toggle (staging/prod). Canvas: flow blocks (Match -> Route -> Split -> Fallback -> Observe). Each block has inline quick-edit. Bottom: code tab (DSL) with sync indicator.
- Match block examples: headers, region, model-capability tags, customer-tier.
- Split block: percentage sliders with live histogram preview.
- Fallback block: chainable list with policy-level timeouts and priority.

3) Test Harness modal: Payload generator presets (chat, embedding, batched calls). Run options: 100/1k/10k synthetic requests, randomized headers/regions. Output: distribution chart, per-variant latency estimate (use profiling heuristics), cost delta estimate, guardrail violations (rate limit, SLA breach, output-quality regression placeholder). Save run as "preview-report".

4) Validation & Safety pane: linter rules (required canary size, max rollback depth), automatic fallback suggestions if a variant's latency > X ms based on historical model. Warnings are actionable links to change blocks.

Backlog grooming (rough priorities):
- M1: editor skeleton + DSL sync (2w) — high impact, must ship for internal alpha.
- M1: test harness basic (100 reqs, deterministic presets) (1w).
- M2: split sliders + histogram + save templates (2w).
- M2: lint rules + auto-fallback generator (1w).
- M3: team-level policy marketplace, clonable templates (3w).
- M3: canary impact estimator with historical telemetry integration (4w, depends on metrics infra).

Acceptance criteria (alpha):
- Author a policy that routes 10% to variant B for 24h, simulate 1k requests, and see expected 10% hit rate in preview.
- DSL editor and visual canvas reflect same policy after edits (two-way sync, no data loss for supported constructs).
- Linter surfaces at least 5 safety warnings and allows quick apply-fix.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- DSL language: extend current rollout JSON or design small YAML/DSL? (Engineering prefers JSON for parsing; PM prefers succinct DSL).
- Simulation fidelity: how closely do we mimic real latency/cost? need discussion with infra/observability.
- Permissions model: who can publish vs who can preview? tie to existing RBAC.

Edge cases & notes to self:
- Nested A/B inside geographic match (EU users split, fallback to smaller model if capacity) — ensure UI can collapse/expand nested branches.
- Keep UI snappy: limit preview runs in staging to protect infra costs. Add sampling guardrails.
- Export policy as JSON for audit logs and versioning.

Next steps / Owners:
- Spike DSL options (Diego) — prototype JSON <> visual mapping (due: 2025-09-17).
- Lightweight harness PoC (Liam) — integrate with local simulator, stubbed metrics (due: 2025-09-24).
- UX mocks (Asha) — mid-fidelity screens for M1, add microcopy for warnings and save flow (due: 2025-09-10).

Meeting notes / references:
- See Linear RW-3214 for feature epic.
- Related GH PR: console#1123 (visual editor prototypes).
- Slack thread: #rollouts: "policy-sandbox-proposal" (link above).

Quick sketch fragments (copyable snippets):
- DSL example (pseudo):
  match: { region: eu, header.X-Tier: premium }
  split: [ { variant: model-v2, pct: 10 }, { variant: model-v1, pct: 90 } ]
  fallback: [ { on_latency_ms: 500, route: model-v1 }, { on_error: true, route: model-safe } ]

Notes-to-self: keep the alpha narrow (no multi-stage rollout UI yet). Prioritize clarity for safety warnings over advanced visual polish.

— Asha
